headerDisplay: Exposes Navien combi boilers and water heaters to HomeKit through the North American NaviLink cloud (`nlus`): hot water and space-heating thermostats, a power switch, recirculation, a fault sensor and temperature probes. Verified on an NCB-240E. Press **Sign in** to list the appliances on your account; every field below can also be edited by hand.
footerDisplay: Your NaviLink password is stored in the Homebridge configuration file, because the plugin has to sign in again after a restart and Navien offers no other credential. See the [documentation](https://github.com/tbaur/homebridge-navilink#readme) for what this plugin does and does not do.

email.title: NaviLink Email
email.description: The email address for your NaviLink account, the same one you use in the NaviLink app.

password.title: NaviLink Password
password.description: Stored in plain text in the Homebridge configuration file, as every Homebridge credential is. It is never written to the Homebridge log.

statusIntervalSec.title: Status Refresh (seconds)
statusIntervalSec.description: A floor on how stale a reading can be. The appliance pushes changes as they happen, so this is not how state normally arrives; it is the backstop for a push that was missed.

readOnly.title: Read-only
readOnly.description: Report everything, change nothing. Every accessory still shows state, and a HomeKit write is declined with one explanatory line in the log.

allowPowerOff.title: Allow HomeKit to Switch the Appliance Off
allowPowerOff.description: Off by default, and worth leaving off. On a combi appliance the power state governs central heating as well as hot water, so "turn off the water heater" said to Siri, or a scene that turns everything off, would stop the heating in a house that may be empty and freezing. With this off, a power-off request is declined and explained instead of obeyed.

diagnosticsInterval.title: Diagnostics Interval (seconds)
diagnosticsInterval.description: Emit a plugin health line to the Homebridge log every N seconds. 0 is off (the default). Allowed range 0–3600; values between 1 and 29 are clamped up to 30. Logs only; nothing is exposed in HomeKit.

structuredLogs.title: Structured (JSON) Logs
structuredLogs.description: When diagnostics are on (diagnosticsInterval > 0), also emit each report as a JSON line next to the human summary. Has no effect while diagnostics are off.

accessoryPrefix.title: Accessory Name Prefix
accessoryPrefix.description: HomeKit tiles become this plus the accessory: "Zone One Hot Water", "Zone One Heating", and so on. Leave blank to use each appliance's own name. Changing it renames the tiles; it does not detach rooms or automations.

id.title: Identity
id.description: Stable identity: twelve hex digits and the channel, as the settings page writes it (lowercase, no separators). Changing it detaches the accessories from their HomeKit rooms and automations.

name.title: Name
name.description: The appliance's name. Accessories are named from it unless options.accessoryPrefix is set: "Boiler" gives "Boiler Hot Water", "Boiler Heating", "Boiler Fault" and so on.

channel.title: Channel
channel.description: 1 for a single appliance. A cascade of several appliances behind one gateway uses a channel each.

dhw.title: Hot Water Thermostat
dhw.description: The domestic hot water setpoint, as a HomeKit thermostat. Reads the outlet temperature. Switching it off does not switch the appliance off unless you also allow that above.

heating.title: Heating Thermostat
heating.description: The space-heating water setpoint, as a HomeKit thermostat. This is the boiler's flow temperature, not a room thermostat: it sets how hot the water going to your radiators is, and your existing room thermostat still decides when heat is called for. Only useful on a combi; an appliance with no heating loop disables it and says so in the log.

power.title: Power Switch
power.description: A switch for the appliance's power state. Switching it off is refused unless "Allow HomeKit to switch the appliance off" is on.

recirculation.title: Recirculation Switch
recirculation.description: Starts the on-demand hot water recirculation pump, so hot water reaches the tap without running it first. The appliance runs the pump for a fixed period and then stops; the switch turns itself off when that happens. Only for appliances with a pump fitted and commissioned.

fault.title: Fault Sensor
fault.description: A contact sensor that opens when the appliance reports an error code, so HomeKit can notify you. The code itself is written to the log.

temperatureSensors.title: Temperature Sensors
temperatureSensors.description: Four read-only sensors: hot water in and out, and heating flow and return. Each one disables itself if the appliance turns out not to report it.

outdoorSensor.title: Outdoor Temperature
outdoorSensor.description: The outdoor probe, on an installation that has one fitted for weather compensation. Most do not.
